<description>
When a low-feerate parent is rejected as `TX_RECONSIDERABLE`, `MempoolRejectedTx` calls `m_txrequest.ForgetTxHash(ptx->GetWitnessHash())` (txdownloadman_impl.cpp:473). For a transaction without witness, wtxid == txid, so this also deletes the txid requests that `MaybeAddOrphanResolutionCandidate` queued for every peer that announced the orphan child.

If the parent then comes from a peer that did not announce the child:

- `Find1P1CPackage` only pairs the parent with children from the same peer, so no package is formed
- the child's announcers are never asked for the parent
- the child stays in the orphanage until some new peer announces it

With a segwit parent the txid differs from the wtxid, so the txid requests survive and the package gets accepted. A legacy (P2PK) parent is affected.

This skips `ForgetTxHash` when the result is `TX_RECONSIDERABLE` and the tx has no witness. New wtxid announcements of that parent are still ignored through `AlreadyHaveTx(include_reconsiderable=true)`. The cost is that announcements already queued may download the parent once more.

The new `test_parent_from_other_peer` in `p2p_opportunistic_1p1c.py` runs for a segwit and a legacy parent: peer A sends the child (orphan), peer B sends the low-fee parent, then it checks that A is asked for the parent by txid and the package is accepted. On master the legacy case times out waiting for that request; with the change it passes. `p2p_orphan_handling.py` and `p2p_tx_download.py` still pass.
</description>

[2026-10-12] c:6121499796 comment by FlashWayne (contributor):
Thanks, agreed it's the same path: the stripped parent in `parent_stripped` and an honest non-segwit parent both reach `ForgetTxHash` with wtxid == txid. The non-segwit case doesn't need an adversary though, a parent relayed by a peer that didn't announce the child is enough.

In case it helps with the catalog: I applied this commit on top of #36437 and stopped setting `holes.parent_stripped`. Without the commit, `p2p_1p1c_liveness` hits the liveness assert within seconds from an empty corpus (964 crashing inputs in 10 minutes); with it, all of those inputs pass, and 5 workers ran for an hour (~13M executions) without a failure. So it looks like it closes that hole. Happy to rebase onto #36437 and drop the flag here, or for you to fold it into #36369/#36437 if you'd rather land them as a group.

@Yudis-bit thanks for testing. I'd keep the txid of a segwit tx out of the reconsiderable filter: a low-feerate copy with a mutated witness also fails as `TX_RECONSIDERABLE`, so it would put the honest parent's txid there, and `AlreadyHaveTx(..., include_reconsiderable=true)` would then ignore txid announcements of the honest parent (the #8279 concern in the comment above that branch). At the line you point to it only affects the early give-up for a child with two reconsiderable parents.
